question: Assume today is 2026-09-01. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total value of online shopping transactions in South Korea in August 2026, in Korean won (KRW), as it will be first reported in the national statistics agency's monthly Online Shopping Trends release (온라인쇼핑동향, National Data Office, formerly Statistics Korea).

target.what: Total value of online shopping transactions (거래액) in South Korea during August 2026, as reported in the National Data Office (formerly Statistics Korea) monthly Online Shopping Trends (온라인쇼핑동향) release — the headline 'online shopping transaction value' aggregate covering all online shopping channels
target.unit: KRW (current prices, total for the month)
target.publisher: 국가데이터처 (National Data Office, formerly 통계청/Statistics Korea) — Online Shopping Trends (온라인쇼핑동향조사)
target.cadence: Monthly, typically released around the first week of the second following month (i.e., August data published early October 2026)
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to the 2026-09-01 cutoff but the official figure is not yet published (release expected ~early October 2026), so this is a genuine forecast. Working interpretation: the headline total online shopping transaction value (거래액) in current KRW, all covered industries,

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 total = most recent published monthly level (e.g., mid-2026) grown by trend monthly growth and adjusted by the historical August seasonal factor (August vs adjacent months). Own history gives both the level anchor and the seasonal shape.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total online shopping transaction value (거래액, all industries, current KRW) for as many months as available up to the cutoff (ideally Jan 2023–Jul 2026), plus the same-month values for August in 2023, 2024, 2025 to estimate the August seasonal factor and year-over-year growth. Minimum: last 12–24 monthly observations and prior August values.
search_hints: Statistics Korea online shopping trends monthly transaction value 2025 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Online shopping is a large, slowly drifting share of total retail sales (소매판매액). Target = total retail sales in August 2026 × online share. Retail sales index/level and the online share provide an independent cross-check on the level.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total retail sales value (소매판매액지수 or 명목 소매판매액) for 2025–mid 2026, and the online-shopping share of retail sales (온라인쇼핑 비중) reported by KOSIS/Statistics Korea. Minimum: recent nominal retail sales level and the online share.

candidates.hypothesis: Total = mobile (모바일) + PC/internet (인터넷) transaction values. Mobile is the dominant and faster-growing component; estimating mobile level and its share, then adding the smaller internet component, gives an alternative decomposition and a consistency check.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly mobile (모바일쇼핑) and internet (인터넷쇼핑) transaction values for 2025–mid 2026, and the mobile share trend. Minimum: latest mobile and internet monthly levels.
search_hints: mobile shopping transaction value Korea monthly

candidates.hypothesis: Total = sum over covered industries (e.g., food & beverages, household goods, fashion, electronics, cosmetics, travel/intermediary services, e-coupons). Summing category-level August 2026 estimates (each grown from its own history) constrains the total and reveals which categories drive August seasonality.
candidates.data_to_find: Category-level (상품군별) monthly online transaction values for 2025–mid 2026, especially the largest categories and travel/intermediary services. Minimum: latest category breakdown with values.
search_hints: Korea online shopping by product category 2026

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 level is affected by nominal consumption growth, inflation in goods, consumer sentiment, and calendar (number of weekend days, Chuseok timing — Chuseok 2026 falls in late September, so August is not boosted by it). Quantify trend growth and any known disruption (e.g., heat waves, policy stimulus, platform changes) to adjust the extrapolation.
candidates.data_to_find: CPI (goods/services) 2025–Aug 2026, household consumption or card spending growth, consumer sentiment index, and any reported e-commerce platform events in mid-2026. Minimum: recent CPI and a consumption growth indicator.

candidates.hypothesis: Analyst or agency forecasts/nowcasts of 2026 online shopping or retail sales growth provide an external anchor for the trend growth rate applied to the last observed level.
candidates.data_to_find: Any published 2026 forecasts for Korean online shopping transaction value or e-commerce market size (e.g., from Statistics Korea, KOSIS, industry reports, or research firms) available before the cutoff. Minimum: one credible growth-rate forecast for 2026.

candidates.hypothesis: Online transaction value ≈ number of online card/payment transactions × average transaction value, or total card spending × online share. Card/payment network aggregates give an independent magnitude check.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly card spending totals and online/e-commerce share of card spending, or payment-network online transaction counts and average ticket, for 2025–mid 2026. Minimum: online card spending level or online share of total card spending.

p1.role: June 2026 total online shopping transaction value (headline aggregate, all channels)

a1.role: ratio of August 2026 level to June 2026 level

methods.rationale: Own-history anchor: June 2026 is the most recent published monthly level (p1). Convert to August 2026 via a seasonal/trend ratio a1 centered at 1.0 with a ±7-8% range. Shared dependency: relies entirely on the June 2026 release being accurate and on no major disruption between June and August. Failure mode: if August is systematically higher or lower than June (seasonal), the ratio assumption is the dominant error source.

p1.role: June 2026 total online shopping transaction value

p12.role: June 2026 year-on-year growth rate (used to back out June 2025 level)

a2.role: August 2026 year-on-year growth rate of online shopping

methods.rationale: YoY route: back out June 2025 level from p1 and p12, then apply an August 2026 YoY growth assumption a2 (centered 9%, range 5-13%) based on the H1/Q2/June 2026 growth run-rate (p13, p14, p12). This implicitly assumes August 2025 ≈ June 2025 level (seasonal flatness), which is a known weakness; the a2 range is widened to absorb some of that. Shared dependency with m1 on p1. Failure mode: if August 2025 was materially different from June 2025, the back-calculation is biased.

a1.role: ratio of August 2026 level to June 2026 level

assumptions.name: August 2026 vs June 2026 online shopping level ratio
assumptions.rationale: June 2026 was described as near a record high (p5 notes June fell 1.7% vs a record May). August typically has no Chuseok boost (Chuseok 2026 is late September) and is a normal summer month; historically August is close to but slightly below June in many years. A ratio centered at 1.0 with ±7-8% range captures both trend growth (June→August ~2 months of ~0.5-0.8%/month nominal growth) and seasonal variation.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert the June 2026 level (p1) to an August 2026 level; assumes no major disruption between June and August 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that August 2026 online shopping was materially boosted or depressed (e.g., a major platform promotion, heat-wave-driven delivery surge, or policy stimulus) relative to June.

assumptions.name: August 2026 YoY growth rate of online shopping
assumptions.rationale: H1 2026 grew 9.6% YoY (p13), Q2 10.1% (p14), June 10.7% (p12). Growth has been accelerating through 2026 from the 4.9% full-year 2025 pace (p19). August 2026 YoY is plausibly near the recent 9-11% run-rate, centered slightly below June's 10.7% to allow mean reversion.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to grow the August 2025 level (derived from p1/p12 back-calculation) to August 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp deceleration or acceleration in mid-2026 online shopping growth (e.g., July 2026 YoY far from 9-11%).

June 2026 was near-record (p5: May was 2nd-highest ever, June -1.7% MoM), so June is a slightly elevated base; two months of trend growth (~+1.5%/mo, from p13/p14) roughly offsets that. August 2026 has no Chuseok boost (Chuseok falls late September 2026); summer heat may lift online grocery/delivery while depressing travel. Centered at 1.0 with a ±7-8% band.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to bridge the June 2026 anchor to August 2026 when no August-specific seasonal factor is available.
assumptions.falsified_by: Historical August-vs-June ratios (2023-2025) showing a systematic deviation from 1.0 beyond the stated band.

assumptions.name: August 2026 year-on-year growth rate of online shopping
assumptions.rationale: H1 2026 +9.6% (p13), Q2 +10.1% (p14), June +10.7% (p12) show acceleration from 2025's +4.9% (p19). August 2026 likely continues the ~9-10% nominal pace, tempered by base effects and CPI running ~3% (p35). Centered at 9% with a wide band.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to project August 2026 from the June 2025 base implied by the June 2026 level and p12.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp deceleration (e.g., July 2026 YoY below 5%) or acceleration above 13%.

assumptions.name: August 2026 vs June 2026 ratio for the mobile-shopping component
assumptions.rationale: Same seasonal bridge as a1 but applied to the mobile component, which has a slightly different seasonal profile (mobile skews to food/delivery, which is less August-sensitive than travel). Slightly wider band than a1.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to bridge the June 2026 mobile anchor to August 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Historical August-vs-June mobile ratios deviating systematically from 1.0.

assumptions.name: Q1 2026 share of H1 2026 online shopping transaction value
assumptions.rationale: p3/p4 are removed, so the Q1/Q2 split must be assumed. assumptions.applies_when: Used to recover the Q2 2026 total (and hence the June monthly level) from the H1 2026 cumulative p2.
assumptions.falsified_by: Publication of the actual Q1 2026 total showing a share outside 0.48-0.51.

methods.label: m1

p2.role: H1 2026 cumulative total online shopping transaction value (Jan-Jun 2026)

a4.role: Q1 2026 share of H1 2026 online shopping transaction value

a5.role: months per quarter (3), converting the Q2 total to a monthly average

a1.role: ratio of August 2026 level to June 2026 level

methods.rationale: Own-history anchor rebuilt without p3/p4: H1 2026 (p2) times the Q2 share (1 - a4) gives Q2 2026, divided by three (a5) gives the June 2026 monthly level, grown by the June-to-August level ratio a1. Largest uncertainty is the missing August seasonal factor; a4 only shifts the level by <1%. Shared dependency: p2 is the same release as p69, so this route is not independent of m2/m3.

methods.label: m2

p69.role: June 2026 total online shopping transaction value (headline aggregate, all channels)

p12.role: June 2026 year-on-year growth rate (used to back out the June 2025 level)

a2.role: August 2026 year-on-year growth rate of online shopping

methods.rationale: YoY route: back out the June 2025 base from the June 2026 level p69 and its YoY rate p12, then apply an August 2026 YoY growth rate a2 grounded in p13/p14/p12. Independent of the June-to-August seasonal assumption; depends instead on the YoY trend holding. Failure mode: if August 2026 YoY diverges sharply from the H1 pace, or if the 2025 base was revised between vintages.
methods.error: input p69: id p69 unknown or discarded

methods.label: m3

p69.role: June 2026 total online shopping transaction value

p14.role: Q2 2026 year-on-year growth rate (proxy for mid-2026 trend)

a1.role: ratio of August 2026 level to June 2026 level

methods.rationale: Trend-adjusted own-history: scale the June 2026 level by the ratio of Q2 trend growth to June growth (p14/p12), then apply the June-to-August level ratio a1. Captures whether June was above or below the quarterly trend. Shares p69, p12 and a1 with m1/m2, so not fully independent.
methods.error: input p69: id p69 unknown or discarded

methods.label: m4

p77.role: June 2026 mobile share of total online shopping transaction value

a3.role: ratio of August 2026 level to June 2026 level for the mobile-shopping component

methods.rationale: Mobile-decomposition cross-check: June mobile value p76 divided by the mobile share p77 recovers the June 2026 total from the mobile side (18.927/0.769 = 24.61tn, matching p69), then apply a3. Because the mobile share is close to 1, this is largely a consistency check on the headline rather than an independent measurement; it mainly guards against a mis-stated June total.

kept.name: August 2026 year-on-year growth rate of online shopping
kept.rationale: H1 2026 +9.6% (p13), Q2 +10.1% (p14), June +10.7% (p12) show acceleration from 2025's +4.9% (p19). August 2026 likely continues the ~9-10% nominal pace, tempered by base effects and CPI running ~3% (p35). Centered at 9% with a wide band.

kept.name: August 2026 vs June 2026 ratio for the mobile-shopping component
kept.rationale: Same seasonal bridge as a1 but applied to the mobile component, which has a slightly different seasonal profile (mobile skews to food/delivery, which is less August-sensitive than travel). Slightly wider band than a1.
kept.applies_when: Used to bridge the June 2026 mobile anchor to August 2026.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
